hops.title: Compare it: a white winter coat on green grass
hops.text: Hold a white winter coat next to a green lawn, and you see the trick right away: a coat that disappears in snow pops out on grass. Many snowshoe hares do that wardrobe swap for real. Over several weeks in fall, they grow white fur in place of their brown summer fur.

sources.citation: Shefferly, N., & Poor, A. (ed.), BioKIDS / Animal Diversity Web, University of Michigan, 'Lepus americanus (snowshoe hare)'

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A white snowshoe hare sitting on a patch of snow beside grass, near a white winter coat on a fence post.
image.caption: A white coat blends right into snow, just like a snowshoe hare's winter fur.

hops.title: Point at it: bumpy tree bark and hidden owls
hops.text: Next time you walk together in a yard or park, stop by a rough tree trunk and look with eyes only. Notice how bark mixes streaks of gray, brown, and shadow. Eastern screech-owls, neighborhood owls only about six inches tall, wear that bark pattern and stretch tall like a branch to blend in.

sources.citation: Smithsonian's National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute, 'Eastern screech-owl'

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A parent and child seen from behind looking up at a rough tree trunk where a tiny gray eastern screech-owl blends into the bark.
image.caption: Rough tree bark is full of streaks and shadows that hide tiny eastern screech-owls in plain sight.

hops.title: Say it: mice don't pick their pajamas
hops.text: “Mice don't pick their pajamas. Their fur color comes from their parents.” Try this line when your child says a worm chose green to hide. Light rock pocket mice blend in on pale rocks. Dark rock pocket mice blend in on dark lava. Neither mouse chose its fur.

sources.citation: Nachman, M. W., Hoekstra, H. E., & D'Agostino, S. L. (2003), 'The genetic basis of adaptive melanism in pocket mice', Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 100(9):5268-5273 (PMID 12704245)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A light tan rock pocket mouse resting on pale rock next to a dark rock pocket mouse resting on black lava rock.
image.caption: Light rock pocket mice blend into pale rock, and dark ones blend into dark lava.
